title: Hostinger or GoDaddy: which web host is worth it once you count the renewal?
seoTitle: Hostinger or GoDaddy: which costs less with renewal?
description: Hostinger or GoDaddy: with SONAR20, Hostinger Premium costs less in the first year and over 4 years. See the math in US dollars and what each plan includes.
metaDescription: SONAR20 takes 20% off a new Hostinger purchase. See the 4-year math against GoDaddy in US dollars, the first year, the renewal and what each plan includes.
imageAlt: The Hostinger logo, a calendar and a renewal icon, with the title Hostinger vs GoDaddy on the band

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: On a new purchase, Hostinger with SONAR20 costs less than GoDaddy both in the first year and over 4 years. GoDaddy's Starter renews for less per year, but its plan list has no domain, email or SSL. The math for each is below, in US dollars.

contentSections.heading: The entry plans side by side
paragraphs: Hostinger's Premium lists a domain and email; GoDaddy's Starter lists neither. GoDaddy's Economy, with 25 GB, lists both, and it is the plan to compare with Premium when the site needs its own address.

contentSections.heading: Hostinger: the price with SONAR20
paragraphs: SONAR20 stacks with the Black Friday price: in the cart, the 48-month Premium dropped from US$95.52 to US$76.42. The code gives 20% off a new purchase and does not apply to the renewal.
Our math: 20% off the page price, the same rule for the other plans. Only Premium was checked in the cart; the others follow the same math.

comparisonTable.caption: Hostinger's international prices on November 6, in US dollars. The SONAR20 columns are our math.

postParagraphs: At renewal, the last column applies, without SONAR20. The code's rules are on the [Hostinger coupon page](/en/coupons/hostinger).

contentSections.heading: Over 4 years, with the renewal
paragraphs: Hostinger wins: 48 months paid at once cover the four years, with no renewal inside that time. GoDaddy only reaches 4 years with three one-year renewals, each at the list price.
postParagraphs: The GoDaddy math does not add Economy's extras after the first year, so its total is the floor. The Deluxe and Ultimate plans, for several sites, are left out: their renewal was not checked in the cart.

contentSections.heading: In the first year, Hostinger also wins
paragraphs: The 12-month Premium costs US$47.88 on the page and US$38.30 with SONAR20. That is US$33.58 less than GoDaddy's Starter, at US$71.88, and US$45.58 less than Economy, at US$83.88.
After the first year, the order changes: Premium renews at US$131.88 a year, Economy at US$143.88 and Starter at US$71.88. Starter renews for less, without a domain, email or SSL on its list.

contentSections.heading: Refunds: 30 days at both
paragraphs: Hostinger accepts a refund request within 30 days of purchase, and GoDaddy's international page also lists a 30-day money-back guarantee. On this point, neither has the edge.

contentSections.heading: What comes with the entry plan
paragraphs: Premium's list also includes weekly backups and a CDN; the page does not list SSL. With GoDaddy's Starter, cPanel comes with the storage, and the rest is left off the list.
With Economy, the cart gives email and SSL free for one year. After that, the SSL auto-renews at US$119.99 a year, and the email is no longer free; the 4-year table adds neither.

contentSections.heading: Which to choose: the verdict
paragraphs: Choose Hostinger if the site will stay online for 4 years: Premium with SONAR20 costs US$76.42 for all four, against US$287.52 for Starter and US$515.52 for Economy, and it lists a domain and email.

Choose GoDaddy Starter if you plan to keep the site well beyond 4 years and need neither a domain nor email: it renews at US$71.88 a year, US$60 below Premium's renewal, but it costs more in the first period.
Choose GoDaddy Economy if you want a domain, email and SSL on the list and accept renewing at US$143.88 a year, more than Premium's renewal.
In all three cases, check the renewal in the cart before paying: promotions can change.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Which is better, Hostinger or GoDaddy? It depends on how long you keep the site. In the first year and over 4 years, Hostinger Premium with SONAR20 costs less than both GoDaddy plans; after that, GoDaddy Starter renews for less. More criteria are in [how to choose a web host](/en/reviews/how-to-choose-web-host-hostinger).

Does GoDaddy renew at the same price? Economy does not: in the cart, the 1-year plan goes back to the list price after the first year, from US$83.88 to US$143.88. Starter has no first-year discount and renews at the same US$71.88.
Does the Hostinger coupon work on the renewal? No: SONAR20 only works on a new purchase. For the renewal, see the [Hostinger renewal guide](/en/reviews/hostinger-renewal-price-coupon-sonar20).

Can I move my site from GoDaddy to Hostinger? Hostinger's help page says free migration covers sites from another company on the Web, Cloud or Agency plans; check your plan with support before cancelling the old one.

contentSections.heading: Who writes this
paragraphs: Em Casa com Cecília runs on Hostinger, and its domain has been registered there since 2024. For GoDaddy, this text uses what its international page and cart show in US dollars.
